text:
incident-bot: [P1] eu-west1 - autoscaler failed to provision nodes in az1; high 5xx spike on hosted inference. PagerDuty alarm fired: INC-20260314-eu1-az1-autoscaler. Runbook: https://goto/runbooks/autoscaler-az-failure

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty created INC-20260314-eu1-az1-autoscaler -> unacked. Routing: primary az1, fallback az2. Notifying on-call SRE rotation.

sara-oncall: acked. I'm on it, starting with autoscaler + nodepool logs. pulling metrics dashboard (latency, 5xx, queue length).

sara-oncall: running quick checks:
```
kubectl -n redwood get hpa
kubectl -n redwood describe nodepool eu-west1-az1
redwoodctl infra autoscaler logs --region eu-west1 --zone az1 --last 30m
```

sara-oncall: logs show repeated errors: "ProviderError: InsufficientCapacity: could not allocate instance" and repeated attach timeouts. Queue backlog for generation-tasks up 320% over baseline.

charlie-eng: looks like a zone-level capacity/spot eviction issue rather than our control plane. Can you confirm cloud provider error codes? if it's InsufficientCapacity we should shift traffic to az2 while provider recovers.

sara-oncall: grabbing raw provider error snippet:
```
2026-03-14T04:05:12Z ERROR autoscaler/allocator.go:149 Provision failed: APIError: InsufficientCapacity: Requested instance type not available in az1
```

bob-sre: I'm joining. sara, can you initiate fallback routing to az2 and open escalation with cloud account team? i'll take on-call handoff after you.

sara-oncall: initiating routing weight change to shift traffic away from az1. command:
```
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west1 --weights az1=10,az2=90 --reason "autoscaler provisioning failures az1"
```

sara-oncall: executed. logs: "routing:update ok - weights applied (az1=10 az2=90)" :white_check_mark: Metrics: az1 qps dropping, az2 qps rising, global 5xx count reducing.

diane-cs: which customers saw errors? need a short blurb for impacted customers and priority list.

sara-oncall: short list: acme-corp (high qps routes) ~20% of requests had 502s between 04:02-04:10 UTC; beta-team (sandbox) also affected. Enterprise customers on dedicated capacity not impacted. I'm preparing a customer impact note for CS.

ops-rotations: recommend enabling degraded-model fallback for non-SLA routes to reduce CPU/latency while az1 recovers. charlie, can we do a quick route-level model downgrade?

charlie-eng: yes — we have a per-route override. applying degraded profile to non-enterprise traffic now:
```
redwoodctl routes patch --selector "tier!=enterprise" --set "model=gpt-small,vram_profile=low" --reason "mitigate az1 capacity spike"
```

sara-oncall: patch applied. telemetry shows token latency drop ~15% and CPU per-instance down. non-SLA 5xx rate fell further.

bob-sre: taking over monitoring. sara, thanks — handoff noted. i'll watch autoscaler events and cloud rep responses. I plan to keep routing weight at az1=10 until autoscaler fully recovers.

sara-oncall: handing off to @bob-sre - my shift out in 8m. notes: autoscaler errors indicate capacity exhaustion in az1; fallback to az2 active; degraded-model fallback enabled for non-enterprise; PD incident updated; customer list attached in CS note.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-20260314-eu1-az1-autoscaler -> acked by sara-oncall at 2026-03-14T04:08:03Z. Escalated to bob-sre at 2026-03-14T04:15:20Z.

bob-sre: cloud provider replied: temporary zone capacity pressure, estimated recovery 20-40m. they have queued capacity requests. Monitoring node join events.

bob-sre: seeing new nodes registering now (12 nodes joined az1 nodepool). verifying pods scheduling + HPA catching up.

charlie-eng: running canary verification on routed traffic: sample response traces look good, 5xx back to baseline.

sara-oncall: thanks all — good handoff.

bob-sre: autoscaler stabilized; provisioning errors stopped around 04:38 UTC. I'll start gradually moving traffic back to default weights:
```
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west1 --weights az1=60,az2=40 --reason "post-recovery gradual shift"
```
`
bob-sre: applied. monitoring for any regression.

charlie-eng: metrics show 5xx at baseline, queue cleared, HPA CPU stable. canary traces good.

pagerduty-bot: INC-20260314-eu1-az1-autoscaler -> resolved by bob-sre at 2026-03-14T04:25:20Z. Post-incident summary: autoscaler failed to provision in az1 due to provider capacity constraints; traffic successfully failed over to az2; degraded-model fallback reduced load on instances; provider restored capacity and nodes rejoined. Root cause: zone-level capacity exhaustion at cloud provider.

sara-oncall: filing post-incident notes and follow-ups: 1) ask cloud rep to confirm why capacity shortfall occurred, 2) review autoscaler retry/backoff logic and instance-type diversification, 3) add automated fallback runbook step to flip routing weights and enable degraded-model fallback.

diane-cs: thanks, will send customer comms for acme-corp + beta-team.

ops-rotations: please add incident to oncall review and ensure runbook tweak is in backlog.

bob-sre: closing thread, will attach metrics + timeline to incident ticket. :wave:
